raw.translational: Understanding the shared pathway of lipoprotein metabolism and the distinct roles of LCAT and APOC2 could lead to targeted therapies for dyslipidemias. For Fish Eye Disease, therapies aimed at improving cholesterol esterification or managing its consequences are relevant. For Familial Apolipoprotein C-II Deficiency, strategies to enhance the activity or availability of functional apolipoprotein C-II or its downstream effects on triglyceride clearance could be explored. Combined insights might also inform broader approaches to managing complex lipid disorders.

**Proposed mechanism:** LCAT (HGNC:6313) —DISRUPTS→ cholesterol esterification and HDL maturation (REACT:R-HSA-173881); cholesterol esterification and HDL maturation (REACT:R-HSA-173881) —DECREASES→ cholesterol esters (CHEBI:17445); cholesterol esters (CHEBI:17445) —LEADS_TO→ corneal opacities (HP:0000604); CETP (HGNC:2345) —DISRUPTS→ cholesterol esterification and HDL maturation (REACT:R-HSA-173881); cholesterol esterification and HDL maturation (REACT:R-HSA-173881) —LEADS_TO→ low HDL cholesterol (HP:0011397); cholesterol esterification and HDL maturation (REACT:R-HSA-173881) —LEADS_TO→ atherosclerosis (HP:0002616). Loss-of-function mutations in LCAT (n1) impair cholesterol esterification and HDL maturation (n3), leading to accumulation of unesterified cholesterol and thus corneal opacities (n5). Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in CETP (n4) also disrupt the normal processing of HDL particles within the cholesterol esterification and HDL maturation pathway (n3), resulting in low HDL cholesterol (n6) and increased risk of atherosclerosis (n7). The convergence is the shared disruption of the cholesterol esterification and HDL maturation pathway (n3).

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in LCAT or CETP with significantly high allele frequencies (>1%) in general population databases like gnomAD would challenge the causal role of these genes in their respective diseases. _(variant: gnomad_v3.1.2)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared pathway of cholesterol esterification and HDL maturation, despite different genetic origins, could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting lipid metabolism for both Fish Eye Disease and CETP deficiency, potentially including interventions aimed at enhancing HDL function or managing dyslipidemia.
